content: Both views capture genuine concerns: presumed consent can increase organ availability and save lives, which many see as a compelling public‑good benefit, while others worry it infringes on individual autonomy by assuming consent without explicit opt‑in. The debate therefore reflects a real clash of values — utilitarian health outcomes versus personal freedom and bodily integrity.
